speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been noticing these skin lesions on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the cluster of painless papules and the recent exposure to a child with similar lesions, can you describe the specific appearance of the bumps on your daughter's skin? Please note if any have a central dimple or if they are grouped in lines.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of pearly, umbilicated papules in a daycare setting is pathognomonic; I will now request images to confirm the typical morphology before finalizing the treatment plan. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of skin lesions.
